segments.title: Welcome & Optimization Foundations
segments.script: Welcome back. Today we examine Gradient Descent, the foundational first-order optimization algorithm that powers modern machine learning.

segments.title: The Objective & Loss Surface J(w)
segments.script: Our objective is to minimize a loss function J of theta, which measures the difference between model predictions and true ground truth targets across parameter space.

segments.title: Learning Rate (Step Size Alpha)
segments.script: The learning rate alpha controls our step size. If alpha is too small, convergence takes forever; if too large, the updates will oscillate or diverge.

segments.title: Gradient Vector & Steepest Descent
segments.script: The gradient vector points in the direction of steepest ascent on the loss surface. Therefore, to minimize error, we take steps in the negative gradient direction.

segments.title: Parameter Update Rule: w_t+1 = w_t - alpha * grad
segments.script: Here is the master parameter update equation: theta at t plus one equals theta at t minus alpha times the gradient of the loss function.

segments.title: Model Training & Convergence Example
segments.script: In training deep neural networks and linear models, repeated mini-batch gradient descent iteratively drives weights toward the global or local minimum.
